deferred_source_units.source_text: of Phalal son of Euzai, opposite the corner, and the upper tower projecting from the king’s house, belonging to the court of the guard. After him was Phadaia son of Phoros.
deferred_source_units.reason: Jeremiah locates a prison court at the king's house, while Nehemiah describes an upper projecting tower belonging to the court of the guard. The shared royal-house setting does not independently identify the same court or establish the tower's location and continuity. This architectural identity remains unresolved.

target_units.text: The king of Babylon’s force had built siegeworks against Jerusalem, and Jeremiah was kept in the prison court at the king’s house.
King Zedekiah had shut him in there, saying, Why do you prophesy, saying, Thus said the Lord: I am handing this city over to Babylon’s king, and he will take it?
